guards: every construction of a Claude client whose request carries a param the cli backend cannot serve — an ALLOWLIST of `model`/`max_tokens`/`messages`, so any other param counts, named or not — has a `{backend:'sdk'}` pin. That is Rule A and no census entry excuses it; the committed `.anthropic-pin-census.json` enumerates the remaining unpinned constructions whose calls carry only serviceable params (Rule B, drift-only)

poisonPill.why: An ordinary helper that builds a Claude client with no backend pin and sends `system`. This gate exists because the refusal it enforces CANNOT FIRE IN CI: the cli backend throws on `system`, CI runs the committed `sdk` default, so an unpinned call is green on every runner and throws only where `CLAUDE_BACKEND=cli` is set — the operator's machine. The break therefore ships, and surfaces one layer up as a model failure rather than a transport one. A merge-time scanner is the only thing that can see it, and a scanner that silently matched nothing would print `clean` over the whole repo and read exactly like a real pass, which is why the decision needs a pill rather than an exemption. The overlay lands on an existing TRACKED script (scripts/anthropic-ping.mjs, itself a declared unpinned site, so the corpus already contains it) rather than a new path, because the harness overlays onto tracked files and because the likelier route in is an existing module growing a Claude call nobody pins. `expectStderr` is the Rule A line specifically: the pill must fail for the UNDECLARED+PARAM reason, not merely exit non-zero — this file is also undeclared once overlaid, and a bare exit check could not tell the two apart. `needsGit` because the corpus is `git ls-files`, not a filesystem walk: the repo, not the disk, decides what this gate reads.
